questions.q: What are the three drop zones in the Chart Data pane?
options: Dataset, Parameter, and Expression
Rows, Columns, and Filters
Category Groups, Series Groups, and Values
Title, Legend, and Axis
questions.explain: Once a Chart data region is selected, the Chart Data pane shows Category Groups, Series Groups, and Values — dragging dataset fields into these areas is what actually builds the chart.

questions.q: What happens if the Series Groups area is left empty?
options: The chart automatically creates one series per category
The chart shows exactly one series, fixed at design time
The chart fails to render
The Values area is disabled
questions.explain: With Series Groups empty, the number of series is fixed at design time — there's only ever one series until you add a field there.

questions.q: How is a Chart data region organized, conceptually?
options: Like a list, with no grouping concept at all
It has no analog to any other data region
Like a matrix — Category Groups maps to columns, Series Groups to rows, Values to the data area
Like a stored procedure, executing top to bottom
questions.explain: A chart is organized like a matrix underneath: Category Groups is like the matrix's Columns group, Series Groups is like its Rows group, and Values is like its Data area.

questions.q: What does dropping a numeric field into the Values area do by default?
options: It's ignored until a Category Group is added
Report Builder aggregates it using the SUM function
The field is displayed unaggregated, row by row
It's converted to a string automatically
questions.explain: By default, a numeric field dropped into Values is aggregated with SUM (non-numeric fields default to COUNT instead, since there's nothing to sum).

questions.q: Which chart types does the New Chart Wizard offer?
options: Only column and pie
Scatter, polar, and stock charts only
Every chart type and sub-type Reporting Services supports
Column, line, pie, bar, and area
questions.explain: The Chart Wizard covers the five most common chart types — column, line, pie, bar, and area. For anything else, such as scatter or polar charts, you add a chart manually and choose from the full Select Chart Type dialog.
